review_notes: ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό → *together* is `noncompositional` with the intervening article `unrepresented`, the reading rule 106 cites and rule 93 requires.

variant_decisions.evidence: Word order of verb and numeral; 'There shall be two women grinding together' renders either.
Presence of the article; ASV 'the one shall be taken' supplies the English article either way.
ASV 'and the other shall be left' renders ἡ δέ and καὶ ἡ alike; ASV regularly gives connective δέ as 'and' in such paired clauses.
ASV has no verse 36 in the text; the mapped textual_variant note at v. 37 ('Some ancient authorities add verse 36 ...') puts the addition in the margin only.

alignments.note: Verb with its supplied subject pronoun, discontinuous around the participle (rule 15).
Vocative noun; the ASV supplies no address word, so no article is in question here.
Verbless clause with an adverbial predicate: the supplied copula rides with the adverb, not with the subject noun (rule 53), discontinuous under rule 15. Placing *is* on σῶμα remains defensible.
The particle takes the *also* the ASV wrote for it (rule 65).
Future passive with auxiliaries; the preverbs' *together* rides inside the verb's own unit, no other token answering to it (rule 106), headed on the verb word.

review_notes: The supplied *is* goes to the adverbial predicate ὅπου under rule 53; the competing placement on σῶμα is named in the unit's note.
The ASV's note on the added verse 36 concerns material outside this projection and affects no unit here.

variant_decisions.evidence: ASV reads 'thither will the eagles also be gathered together'; 'also' renders καί, which the RP reading lacks.
